searchText: <@!203220829473996800> can confirm that Teku considers valid any message with signature and pubkey being the points at infinity in the respective subgroups. I can't find anything in the IETF draft that covers this case, and the math checks out, so I'm assuming this makes sense. There doesn't seem to have been a fork on Witti, and the validator has been inducted, so it looks like Teku, LH and Prysm all agree about this. witti.beaconcha.in is currently down, might take a bit :p hm both our prysm witti nodes are unable to find any peers which is why the explorer is currently not syncing ``` prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-06 17:45:31" level=info msg="Waiting for enough suitable peers before syncing" prefix=initial-sync required=1 suitable=0 prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-06 17:45:36" level=info msg="Waiting for enough suitable peers before syncing" prefix=initial-sync required=1 suitable=0 prysm-node-witti | time="2020-06-06 17:45:41" level=info msg="Waiting for enough suitable peers before syncing" prefix=initial-sync required=1 suitable=0 ``` <@!471975503859810316> Hmm, if you can save the latest logs before trying a restart that would be nice just before the explorer went down, teku client didn't propose any blocks for a while. Is anyone running one except <@!573787335796326400> ? I’m running three teku nodes. There was a period around 2am UTC where witti went 40 epochs without finalising. We’re still working to avoid memory growth during nonfinalisation. Two of my nodes struggled, one restarted a couple of times before finality was restored and they went back to normal. The third node is on my recent code and sailed through without an issue which Is nice I changed my graffiti, so I don't show up there... I'll check my logs in the morning. Late here now. I know that Afri's Teku validators have been down for a week now. Validators 53 to 62 are mine which is the box that restarted a few times.

excerpts.content: <@!203220829473996800> can confirm that Teku considers valid any message with signature and pubkey being the points at infinity in the respective subgroups. I can't find anything in the IETF draft that covers this case, and the math checks out, so I'm assuming this makes sense. There doesn't seem to have been a fork on Witti, and the validator has been inducted, so it looks like Teku, LH and Prysm all agree about this.
